sections.h2: Where is Bountiful, Utah, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Bountiful is a city in Davis County, Utah, built on the slope between the Wasatch Range and the Great Salt Lake flats. Its elevation is about 4,771 feet, and the city covers roughly 13 square miles.

The original downtown sits at the base of the mountains. Homes climb the benches to the east, and the land to the west is flat and runs out toward the lake. Most of the ground east of the city is U.S. Forest Service land, so the hillside streets end where public land begins.

North Salt Lake lies to the south, Woods Cross and West Bountiful to the west, and Centerville to the north. Val Verda is the name used for the area in the southern part of the city. A seller on a bench street and a seller on the west side are dealing with very different lots, and buyers know it.

sections.h2: How did Bountiful start, and how fast has it grown?
sections.html:
Perrigrine Sessions and his family settled the site on September 27, 1847, which made it the second settlement in Utah after Salt Lake City. The place was first called Sessions Settlement and North Canyon Ward, and it was renamed Bountiful in 1855. The city incorporated in 1892, and electric lights came in 1907.

Growth was slow for a long time and then fast. The census counted 6,004 residents in 1950 and 17,039 in 1960. Bountiful was the largest city in Davis County until 1985, when Layton passed it.

The 2020 count came with 15,427 households and 15,945 housing units, and a median age of 35.1. Few lots are left to build on, so most sales here are resales of houses that already have decades of wear.

sections.h2: What does Bountiful's climate and terrain mean for a house?
sections.html:
Bountiful has a dry climate with about 23 inches of precipitation and about 59 inches of snow in a typical year. The record high is 104 degrees and the record low is minus 9, so roofs, furnaces and cooling systems all get used.

Heavy snow matters most on older roofs and on shaded driveways. Buyers and inspectors in a snow climate often look at the roof surface, the attic insulation and the gutters first. A seller who has not touched those in years should expect questions.

The Wasatch Fault runs along the base of the range, and the Utah Division of Emergency Management says more than 85 percent of Utahns live in the earthquake zone along the Wasatch Front. The same agency notes that unreinforced masonry buildings are a major concern along the fault. If your Bountiful house is older brick, a buyer may ask about chimneys, foundations and any past retrofit work.

  • Roof age and snow load on the east benches
  • Brick chimneys and masonry walls on older homes
  • Water drainage on steeper hillside lots
  • Furnace and water heater age

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and rail serve Bountiful?
sections.html:
Davis School District serves Bountiful. The nine elementary schools serving the city are Adelaide, Boulton, Bountiful, Holbrook, Meadowbrook, Muir, Oak Hills, Tolman and Valley View. The junior highs are Bountiful, Millcreek, Mueller Park and South Davis.

Interstate 15 is the main road, and the FrontRunner commuter rail has served Bountiful since April 2008. The Legacy Parkway opened on September 13, 2008, to take pressure off I-15. The narrow gap into Salt Lake County still causes slow traffic at rush hour, which is a talking point for buyers who commute south.

Other local anchors include Lakeview Hospital, the Bountiful Utah Temple (dedicated in 1995) and Mueller Park Canyon with its popular trail. Houses within a short drive of the canyon trailheads tend to get extra attention from buyers who hike.

sections.h2: Who provides power and water in Bountiful, and what do you do at move-out?
sections.html:
Bountiful City runs its own electric department, and it also handles utility billing. The power office is at 198 South 200 West, and the 24-hour outage line is 801-298-6072. Utility billing is at 801-298-6100.

The city's utility page says you must speak with a utility representative to start or end service, so a seller should call before the closing date rather than relying on an online form. City Hall is at 795 South Main Street. Final meter readings and the last bill are easier to sort out when the date of the sale is already fixed.

  • Call 801-298-6100 to schedule the end of your service
  • Ask for a final meter reading on the closing date
  • Confirm where the final bill should be mailed
  • Keep a copy of the closed account for your records

sections.h2: How are Bountiful property taxes billed and paid?
sections.html:
Bountiful property tax is billed by Davis County, and the bill is due November 30 each year. If that date lands on a weekend, it moves to the next business day. The county treasurer's office is at 61 South Main Street, Room 105, in Farmington, and the phone number is 801-451-3243.

Utah taxes a primary residence at a reduced share of value. Under Utah Code 59-2-103, residential property gets a 45 percent reduction, so only 55 percent of market value is taxed. The reduction covers no more than one acre of land per residential unit.

If a lender escrows your taxes, the lender may pay through a third-party service, and the county notes that can delay posting by several days. Check the account before you list.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Bountiful home value in Davis County?
sections.html:
You file a Board of Equalization appeal with the Davis County Controller by the deadline printed on your Notice of Property Market Valuation. The county's online form takes one application per parcel, and it asks you to state your own opinion of the value as of January 1.

The county lists the kinds of evidence it accepts. A recent closing statement, a full appraisal, at least three comparable sales within one mile, an income statement, a documented factual error or a record of a damaged condition can each support a case. Only the current year's market value can be appealed, not the tax rate. The controller's phone number is 801-451-3323.

If you sell mid-year, the appeal and the tax bill still follow the property. Tell the buyer's side what is pending so the title company can handle any refund correctly.

sections.h2: What do Bountiful sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
Sellers in Bountiful most often deal with an older house, a hillside lot, or a buyer who needs a quick, simple closing. A cash sale removes the lender appraisal and the repair negotiation that often follow a listing, and it lets you pick the closing date.

  • Older homes that need roof, electrical or plumbing work before a retail buyer will lend
  • Inherited houses where several family members have to agree before anyone signs
  • Rentals with tenants in place and a lease that runs past the sale date
  • Overdue repairs that make a traditional listing hard to price

Bountiful's resale pool is large because the city is close to Salt Lake City and has the FrontRunner line. That helps a well-kept house on the market. It does less for a property that needs work, which is where an as-is sale tends to fit.

faqs.q: What county is Bountiful, Utah in, and who bills the property tax?
faqs.a: Bountiful is in Davis County, and the Davis County treasurer bills and collects the property tax. The office is at 61 South Main Street in Farmington, and the phone number is 801-451-3243.

faqs.q: When is Bountiful property tax due?
faqs.a: Property tax in Bountiful is due November 30. If that date falls on a weekend, Davis County moves the deadline to the next business day. A late payment carries a penalty of the greater of $10 or 2.5 percent per parcel.

faqs.q: Is there a way to lower the taxable value on a Bountiful house?
faqs.a: A primary residence already gets the 45 percent residential reduction under Utah Code 59-2-103. If you think the market value on your valuation notice is too high, you can file a Board of Equalization appeal with the Davis County Controller by the date printed on the notice.

faqs.q: Who do I call to stop electric service when I sell?
faqs.a: Call Bountiful City utility billing at 801-298-6100. The city says you must speak with a representative to start or end service, so schedule it before closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bountiful house that has tenants or needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Houses with tenants, deferred repairs or an inherited title can be sold as they are. Tell the buyer about the lease terms and the condition up front so the closing date and any move-out terms are clear.
